news.title: India U-15 secure 87th place finish in FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026 in Baku
news.lede: Blue Colts scored 30 goals across 10 games The FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival 2026 kicked off in Baku, Azerbaijan, a week ago, and after ten games, India U-15 finally wrapped their campaign in Baku with a 6-4 victory against Cuba to finish 87th among 189 teams from the length and breadth of this planet. India U-15 were drawn in Group K, and until the final matchweek, India were the sole unbeaten team in the group and favourites to top the group and qualify for Tier A. The Blue Colts, led by Bibiano Fernandes, had an impressive campaign and too many moments to cherish in Baku. From trailing 2-0 down against Trinidad and Tobago to clinching a 3-2 comeback win, upsetting African heavyweight Cameroon 2-1 to a four-goal masterclass from Victor Lalawmpuia, the Blue Colts can be proud of their efforts as the team sealed their Baku journey on an exhilarating note against Cuba.

news.title: Ireland U15s wrap up World Cup with win against Wales
news.lede: The Republic of Ireland Under-15s concluded their FIFA Men’s World Cup with a 3-2 win over Wales in Baku to finish 21st overall in Tier A. The inaugural tournament was played in an 8v8 format, with two 20-minute halves in each game. Ireland brought a 14-player squad to Azerbaijan where they faced opposition from five different continents. Across 10 games in six days, Ireland defeated Montenegro, Zimbabwe, England, Cambodia, Northern Ireland, Cameroon and Cymru.

England’s Under-15 World Cup campaign in Azerbaijan witnessed further drama on Friday after they secured a 3-2 victory over Bolivia courtesy of an uncontested late penalty.

news.title: Kyrgyzstan secures 52nd place at FIFA U15 World Cup Festival in Azerbaijan
news.lede: The Central Asian nation concludes its campaign in the 8-a-side tournament, navigating a complex division structure against 189 global teams. Kyrgyzstan's under-15 national football team has finished 52nd out of 189 participating teams at the FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival in Azerbaijan, concluding a demanding campaign in the global youth tournament. The festival utilized an unusual 8-a-side format played on reduced-size pitches, a structure designed by FIFA to maximize player touches and accelerate tactical decision-making in tight spaces. This environment forces young athletes to develop technical proficiency and spatial awareness much faster than the traditional 11-a-side game, serving as a critical incubator for future talent.

news.title: Fifa to miss equal Women’s World Cup prize money ambition set by Infantino
news.lede: Infantino said in 2023 equality was Fifa’s target. Prize money could double but big gap will remain. Fifa is to fall short of gender equality with the prize money on offer at next year’s Women’s World Cup, despite making a record $15bn (£11.2bn) in revenue from this summer’s men’s tournament. Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s ambitionwas to have equality for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.”

news.title: India ends FIFA U-15 World Cup 2026 campaign with 2-1 win over Cuba
news.lede: Baku India ended its campaign at the FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026 on a winning note, defeating Cuba 6-4 in the 87th-place play-off at the Hovsan Competition Complex Pitch 1B in Baku on Friday, October 30, 2026. Victor Lalawmpuia, Nibas Meetei Wahengbam and R. Lalremruatfela scored twice each as the Blue Colts won their 10th and final fixture of the tournament. India built a commanding 6-1 advantage before Cuba struck three late goals to narrow the margin.

news.title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup: Flamingos’ celebration goes viral after victory

Nigeria's U-17 women's football team, the Flamingos, booked a quarterfinal spot at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup after a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Mexico in their Round of 16 clash on Thursday, with the players' on-pitch celebration quickly going viral. Head coach Hakeem Busari's side took the lead just before the break, when Oluebube Umejiaku found the net in the 40th minute to give Nigeria a 1-0 advantage at half-time. As seen on CAF's official website, Nigeria continued to push after the restart and were rewarded in the 72nd minute when Mary Akpan Dunstan scored to double the lead.

news.title: PH 110th of 189 nations in 2026 FIFA U15 World Cup
news.lede: BAKU – The Philippine Under-15 Men’s National Football Team (PMNFT U15) concluded its maiden FIFA World Cup & Festival at a respectable 110th place out of 189 countries in the world’s biggest football tournament in terms of participation here. This came after a dramatic final match between the Philippines and Andorra, with the European side winning, 2-1 off a late goal. It was an exchange of goals in the opening two minutes, with Andorra’s Max Rossell scoring an Olimpico from the left corner kick 23 seconds in, but Filipino winger Sylar Alcantara respondent a minute later with a long shot from midfield to tie the game. PMNFT U15 had the more dangerous chances on goal but Andorran goalkeeper Joan Caballol was a tough nut to crack between the sticks.
